# Getting started

## Your first few minutes

Signing up needs nothing more than an email and a password. You're in straight
away — you can fill in the rest of your profile whenever you like.

Once you confirm your email, Aevum will ask for a few details — your name, and the
country you're in (which sets your currency). You can add these now or skip them for
later; either way, that's the moment Aevum sends your welcome email and greets you
by name.

From there, a short first-run checklist points you at the things that make Aevum
useful: adding an account, importing a statement, and setting a budget or two. It
shows once, and once you've worked through it — or dismissed it — it stays out of
your way.

## See Aevum with real data first

An empty budgeting app is hard to judge. The whole point of Aevum is the picture
that appears _after_ your spending is in it — the weekly tax, the budgets, the
savings building up. So before you add anything of your own, you can explore a
fully-populated version.

**A live preview.** Even before you commit to anything, you can look around a
complete, working Aevum — a realistic few months of spending, budgets, weekly bills
and savings already in place. It's a genuine walk-through of every screen, so you can
see exactly what Aevum does with real activity rather than reading about it.

**Sample data in your own account.** When you're signed in and haven't added
anything yet, you can load a set of sample transactions into your own account with a
single tap. This isn't a mock-up bolted on the side — it's run through exactly the
same machinery your real spending would be, so the categories, the weekly tax bills
and the savings pot all behave the way they will once your own data lands. It's the
best way to get a feel for the app before importing a statement.

The sample world spans about three months of everyday spending — salary coming in,
groceries and fuel and dining out going back out, a few monthly subscriptions and
EMIs — and it's always kept current, so the most recent activity lands on today
rather than looking months old.

## Starting fresh when you're ready

The sample data is clearly flagged as sample data the whole time it's loaded, so you
never confuse it with the real thing. When you're ready to begin for real, clearing
it out takes a single step — no password, no ceremony, because there's nothing of
yours to protect yet.

The one moment that changes is if you've already started adding your own
transactions on top of the sample set. At that point Aevum won't quietly wipe
everything — it asks you to confirm properly first, so your real data is never lost
by accident.

Clearing the sample data only clears the data. Where you are in your setup journey —
what you've filled in, what you've dismissed — stays exactly as it was, so you pick
up right where you left off.

## What comes next

Once the sample data is gone, Aevum is yours and empty, ready for the real thing.
Add an account, import a statement or enter a few transactions by hand, and the same
picture you just explored starts filling in with your own life.
